subject: KEK derivation audit and transport checklist - BlueHarbor request
messages:
From: Maya Levin <compliance@blueharbor.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@blueharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: KEK derivation, transport logs and rotation artifacts

Hi Priya,

We're finalizing the SIG/SOC2 evidence package for BlueHarbor's onboarding. A few items we still need from Redwood around key management for tenant-encrypted workloads:

- KEK/DEK derivation description and the algorithm used (high level, include key derivation function and any HKDF/salted steps).
- Export of rotation events for the last 12 months (key IDs, timestamps, actor, reason).
- A sanitized transport log extract that shows wrapped-key exports and their transport-side handshake success/failure codes (we only need headers, not payload).
- HSM attestation or vendor-signed statement for the HSM pool that handles tenant wrapping (most recent).
- A short note on in-transit protections for key material and any time-limited ephemeral wrapping used for transit.

Can you provide the above by EOD Thursday Pacific? If any items need redaction, let us know your recommended scrub rules. Also, if there's a short MMP (mutual action plan) we should follow for accepting artifacts, please attach.

Thanks,
Maya Levin
Senior Compliance Manager
BlueHarbor Financial

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Maya Levin <compliance@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@blueharbor.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:10:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: KEK derivation, transport logs and rotation artifacts

Hi Maya — thanks for the note and welcome again. We're prioritizing this and can deliver a scrubbed package plus an attached MMP. High-level plan:

1) Deliverables by Thu EOD PT:
   - kek-rotation-events-2026-2027.csv (rotation table: key_id, rotated_at, rotated_by, reason, version)
   - transport-log-extract-202704.zip (sanitized; includes only headers, handshake codes, and timestamps)
   - hsm-attestation-2027-03.pdf (vendor-signed statement; redacted serials per below)
   - a 1-page KEK derivation overview (algorithm, KDF, salt handling, wrap/unwrap flow)

2) Scrub rules we propose: remove raw key material, replace tenant_ids with deterministic pseudonyms, truncate HSM serials to last 4 hex chars, and redact operator usernames but include role and team.

3) Proposed transfer: secure Drive folder + one-time link, and we can provide an optional PGP-signed checksum and HubSpot record for traceability.

Jonas and Irene — tagging you for the rotation export and attestation pull.

Maya — are you happy with the scrub rules above? If so, we'll begin exports and share a secure link when ready.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Compliance & GTM Security
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Levin <compliance@blueharbor.com>, Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@blueharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:02:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: KEK derivation, transport logs and rotation artifacts

Priya / Irene — quick notes from infra side:

- I'll export rotation events from the key-management audit store (we'll include key_id, event_type, actor_role, rotation_reason, and a redacted actor_id).
- For transport logs, we will include handshake status codes, source/dest IPs (CIDR /24), and transport timestamps. No payloads.
- HSM attestation: vendor provided an attestation PDF (FIPS/HSM tamper evidence) — we will redact full serials but include a certificate fingerprint and the attestation date.
- KEK derivation doc: will include KDF (HKDF-SHA256), salt rotation cadence, and how tenant-specific derivation works (no secrets in doc).

Irene — please prepare the zip and the csv and drop in a secure folder. I'll run the scrub job and generate checksums.

Jonas
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Maya Levin <compliance@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@blueharbor.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:04:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: KEK derivation, transport logs and rotation artifacts

Hi Maya / Hector — attached is the sanitized package we discussed. Items delivered:

- kek-rotation-events-2026-2027.csv (attached)
- transport-log-extract-202704.zip (attached)
- hsm-attestation-2027-03.pdf (attached)
- KEK-Derivation-Overview.txt (1 page, in Drive link below)

Delivery notes:
- We redacted raw key material and replaced tenant IDs with pseudonyms (TH-xxxxx).
- HSM serial numbers are truncated to the last 4 hex characters; cert fingerprints included for traceability.
- The transport extract contains handshake response codes (0 = success, 1 = timeout, 2 = mismatch) and the wrapped-key operation identifiers. No payloads or wrapped key blobs were included.

Secure link (expires in 7 days): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_share/KEK-Exports
HubSpot evidence record: HS-483912

If you want a short recorded walkthrough (15 min) of the CSV fields and scrub rules, let me know times that work and we'll set up a calendar invite.

Attachments: kek-rotation-events-2026-2027.csv (attachment stub), transport-log-extract-202704.zip (attachment stub), hsm-attestation-2027-03.pdf (attachment stub)

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Compliance & GTM Security
Redwood Inference

From: Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@blueharbor.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Maya Levin <compliance@blueharbor.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:07:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: KEK derivation, transport logs and rotation artifacts

Thanks, Priya — we received the link and the stub attachments. Quick clarifying questions before we onboard the artifacts into our evidence tracker:

- In the KEK-Derivation-Overview you mention a 90-day salt rotation for tenant derivation; can you confirm whether that cadence is automated or manual?
- For the transport codes, does the "1 = timeout" category also include transient network route changes, or only server-side handshake timeouts? We want to map which events could indicate potential in-transit failures.

If you can reply briefly we can close this item. If easier, a 10-min call would also do.

Regards,
Hector Ramos
Sr. InfoSec Engineer
BlueHarbor Financial
